analytic.title: DYFARS: Boosting Reliability in Fault-Tolerant Heterogeneous Distributed Systems Through Dynamic Scheduling

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: In this paper, we propose a dynamic and reliabilitydriven real-time fault-tolerant scheduling algorithm on heterogeneous distributed systems (DYFARS). Primary-backup copy scheme is leveraged by DYFARS to tolerate both hardware and software failures. Most importantly, DYFARS employs reliability costs as its main objective to dynamically schedule independent, non-preemptive aperiodic tasks, therefore system reliability is enhanced without additional hardware costs. A salient difference between our DYFARS and existing scheduling approaches is that DYFARS considers backup copies in both active and passive forms; therefore, DYFARS is more flexible than the existing scheduling schemes in the literature. Finally, simulation experiments are carried out to compare DYFARS with existing similar algorithm, experiment results show that DYFARS is superior to existing algorithm regarding both Schedulability and Reliability.

div.head: Introduction
div.p: In the past decade, heterogeneous distributed systems have been widely used for many real-time safety-critical applications like avionic control and nuclear control systems with the growing needs of building reliable real-time applications. In real-time systems, the correctness of the systems depends not only on the results of a computation, but also on the time at which these results are produced. Catastrophic consequences will inevitably occur if real-time tasks fail to ensure correct results before deadlines. Due to the critical nature of the safety-critical applications, it is of paramount importance to provide high reliability and fault-tolerance for real-time tasks in heterogeneous systems.

In order to achieve high performances for realtime heterogeneous systems, much attention has been paid to real-time scheduling algorithms based on heterogeneous systems. Ranaweer and Agrawal developed a scheduling scheme named SDTP for heterogeneous systems [1]. Reliability cost was factored in some scheduling algorithms for tasks with precedence constraints [2] [3]. Although schedulability is a main objective of these scheduling algorithms, the algorithms neither consider timing constraints nor support fault-tolerance. In addition, reliability models in these studies are geared to handle aperiodic, nonpreemptive tasks.

Fault-tolerance is an essential requirement of realtime systems, which can be achieved in several approaches. One efficient fault tolerant technique, definitely, is scheduling algorithms, among which the Primary-backup scheme plays a key role. In this approach, two versions of one task are scheduled on two different processors and an acceptance test is used to check the correctness of schedules [4,5,6,11]. Three variants of the primary-backup approach include (1) the active-backup-copy-based schemes [4], (2) the passive-backup-copy-based schemes [5], and (3) the primary/backup-copy overlapping techniques [6]. Generally, backup copy is always preferred to be executed as passive backup copy, because it can take the advantages of backup copy overloading and backup copy de-allocation technique to improve schedulability [4,5]. Primary backup copy overlapping technique is a tradeoff technique between the other two can explore the advantages of both the other two approaches [6,11].

Both active backup copies and passive backup copies have been incorporated into the Rate-Monotonic First-Fit assignment algorithm to provide faulttolerance [7]. This approach overcomes the drawbacks of timing constraints on backup copies to some extends. However, this scheduling algorithm neither considers heterogeneous systems nor takes system reliability into account.

Real-time fault-tolerant scheduling algorithms based on heterogeneous distributed systems have been extensively studied by Qin et.al [8,9,10]. The algorithms proposed in [8,9] are based on heterogeneous distributed systems and take reliability as their main scheduling objective, but these algorithms are static in nature and only support one type of backup copy. Recently, we constructed a novel reliability model for real-time periodic tasks running in fault-tolerant heterogeneous systems [14]. According to this reliability model, we developed a real-time fault-tolerant algorithm (referred to as RDFTAHS) for heterogeneous systems. RDFTAHS aims at boosting reliability while guaranteeing timing requirements of periodic tasks. Although reliability model in RDFTAHS consider both active and passive backup copy, RDFTAHS is also static in nature and only support periodic tasks. Qin proposed a reliabilitydriven dynamic scheduling algorithm, DRCD, based on heterogeneous systems [10]. However, the tasks in DRCD are presented in the form of DAG (Directed acyclic graph). Actually, in realistic world, most of the tasks are in the form non-preemptive and aperiodic and without precedence constrains. In addition, DRCD does not take fault-tolerance into account. Dynamic fault-tolerant scheduling algorithms are also extensively studied these years [11,12,13]. However, a common drawback of theses algorithms proposed in [11,l2,13] is that they only support one type of backup copy.

Although numerous algorithms have been developed with respect to real-time fault-tolerant scheduling for distributed systems, to the best of our knowledge no work has been done on reliability-driven real-time fault-tolerant scheduling tailored for aperiodic non-preemptive tasks for heterogeneous distributed systems that take both active and passive copy into account.

In this study, the major contributions include: 1. A novel fault-tolerant reliability model for aperiodic tasks is proposed by extending the conventional reliability model designed for non faulttolerant tasks;

2. The primary backup copy approach is leveraged to tolerate single processor failures; DYFARS considers both active and passive backup copies, which remedy the deficiency of only one type of backup copy supported by existing algorithms;

3. A dynamic and reliability-driven real-time fault-tolerant scheduling algorithm on heterogeneous distributed systems(DYFARS) which employs reliability costs as its main objective to dynamically schedule independent, non-preemptive aperiodic tasks, therefore system reliability is enhanced without additional hardware costs; 4. Finally, simulation experiments are carried out to compare DYFARS with existing similar algorithms, results shows that DYFARS is superior to existing algorithms regarding both Schedulability and Reliability;

The roadmap of this paper is organized as follows: In section 2, a system model and related assumptions are presented. Section 3 proposes a reliability model for our systems model. A novel real-time fault-tolerant scheduling algorithm is outlined in Section 4. Simulation experiments and performance analysis are presented in section 5. Finally, Section 6 concludes the paper by summarizing the main contribution of this paper and commenting on future directions of this work.

div.head: Reliability Model
div.p: Srinivasan and Jha defined reliability of a system with respect to a task set as the probability that the system can run the task set without any failure [2]. The concept of reliability in their study relies on reliability cost. It should be noted that the reliability cost of a task on a processor is a product of the task execution time and the failure rate of the processor. The reliability cost used in their study is defined for a set of aperiodic tasks that are non-preemptive in nature. In addition, a major drawback of current reliability mode based on aperiodic, non-preemptive tasks is that they only consider backup copy in active or passive form. We attempt to address the issue of reliability that takes both active and passive backup copies into account.
A processor might fail during an idle time, but it is assumed that processors' failures during an idle time interval are not considered in our reliability model [13,14].

With the above two assumptions along with the single processor failure assumption, we can safely only consider the system reliability in fault-free scenario. Moreover, we only need to consider the effects of processors failure on tasks while processor is working. div.head: Scheduling Strategies
div.p: According the definition of reliability costs, we propose a dynamic and reliability-driven real-time fault-tolerant scheduling algorithm on heterogeneous distributed systems (DYFARS). DYFARS employs reliability costs as its main objective to dynamically schedule independent, non-preemptive aperiodic tasks, therefore system reliability is enhanced without additional hardware costs. DYFARS adapts an admission control mechanism to schedule dynamically arriving tasks. If the tasks are unable to be scheduled by our algorithm, we will reject it. The scheduling policies can be concluded as following: 1. Try to assign primary copy to a processor on which the reliability cost is minimal. 2. Try to schedule backup copy as a passive copy whenever possible. 3. If a backup copy has to be scheduled as an active backup copy, the algorithm endeavors to assign backup copy to a processor on which the reliability costs is minimal.

div.head: The Scheduling Algorithm
div.p: DYFARS leverages the Primary Backup Copy scheme to achieve fault-tolerance. When a task copy j i arrives at heterogeneous systems, a corresponding backup copy v i is produced. The backup copy is scheduled after the primary copy. According to our scheduling strategies, we should try to assign the primary copy to the processor on which its reliability cost is minimal and follow the ASAP (as soon as possible) strategy. As for the backup copy, DYFARS makes an effort to make it executed as passive status. If a backup copy has to be executed as an active status, DYFARS endeavors to allocate it to a processor to minimize the reliability costs introduced (namely, rc = [ ] DC i,k * k λ ,where ( ) i k P j P = ). div.head: Performance Evaluation
div.p: In this section, a number of simulations are carried out to compare the DYFARS algorithm with the algorithm DRFTBOA (Dynamic real-time faulttolerant backup copy algorithm) proposed in [12]. To make our comparison fair and meaningful, we make some modifications DRFTBOA so that DRFTBOA has been adapted to heterogeneous systems.

div.head: Experimental Platform
div.p: The heterogeneous distributed systems can be characterized by the following parameters.

1. Processor in heterogeneous distributed systems is denoted by M，ranging in the time interval [4,18], the default value is 10 [9,10]； 2. The processor failure rates λ follows poison process, which is uniformly distributed from 0.95× 10 - 6 /hour(10 -4 ) to 1.05*10 -6 /hour(10 -4 ) [9,10]；
The tasks in simulations are generated according to:
1. The execution time of each task copy on every processor is uniformly distributed in time interval Min_E and Max_E;
2. The relative deadline of real-time tasks is δ times of the maximal actually execution time;

3. The tasks arrival rate is uniformly distributed from 5×10 -4 No/Sec to 25× 10 -4 No/Sec. Two performance metrics are used to capture there aspects of real-time fault-tolerant scheduling. The first metric is Reliability Costs, defined in (5); The second one is Schedulability, defined to be the guaranteed ration of acceptance tasks as (10).

div.head: Performance Comparisons
div.p: First, we compare DYFARS and DRFTBOA with respect to reliability costs, the processor number is fixed to 8 and tasks arriving rate is set to 15×10 -4 NO/.Sec. Fig. 1. shows the impact of the task set size on the reliability costs of the two algorithms. It is clear that the reliability costs of both algorithms proportionally increase with the increasing of task set size L. This is because when the number tasks increases, more processors time are required to guarantee the deadlines of tasks, which leads to an increase of the reliability costs. Most importantly, it is revealed that DYFARS can remarkably reduce the reliability costs compared to DRFTBOA. This is because DYFARS makes an effort to minimize the reliability costs while DRFTBOA ignores reliability while scheduling task.

div.head: Figure.1. Comparison of the Reliability Costs between DYFARS and DRFTBOA
div.p: Fig. 2.shows the schedulability performance of the two algorithms for the experiments conducted in section 5.2. It was noted that schedulability of both algorithm decreases proportionally with the size of tasks, this is because with the number of tasks increases, processors time will be occupied by more tasks, therefore, more tasks will be rejected, which leads to a drop of GR. However, it is noted that DYFARS is still superior to DRFTBOA in terms of schedulability, this phenomenon can be explained by the fact DYFARS can take the advantages of the passive backup copies to enhance schedulability

div.head: Summary and Future works
div.p: In this paper, we presented a novel reliability model for aperiodic and non-preemptive tasks based on faulttolerant real-time heterogeneous distributed systems. Next, we propose a dynamic and reliability-driven realtime fault-tolerant scheduling algorithm on heterogeneous distributed systems (DYFARS). DYFARS employs reliability costs as its main objective to dynamically schedule independent, non-preemptive aperiodic tasks, therefore system reliability is enhanced without additional any hardware cost. DYFARS considers both active and passive backup copies, which remedy the deficiency of only one type of backup copy supported by existing algorithms.
Simulation experiments are carried out to compare DYFARS with existing similar algorithm, results shows that DYFARS is superior to existing algorithm in terms of both Schedulability and Reliability.
In our future works, we intend to study more efficient scheduling algorithms in the context of heterogeneous distributed systems.
